props.title: The Last Mountain
props.initialSlug: Documentary about mountain top removal mining

sections.content: **The Last Mountain** (2011) stands as a pivotal environmental documentary that exposes the devastating impact of mountaintop removal coal mining in Appalachia. Director Bill Haney crafts a compelling narrative that follows Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and local activists fighting against Massey Energy in Coal River Valley, West Virginia. The film shares DNA with other hard-hitting environmental docs like **Gasland** (2010) and **An Inconvenient Truth** (2006), but distinguishes itself through intimate portraits of community resistance and stark footage of environmental destruction.

sections.content: The environmental documentary landscape shifted dramatically in the 2000s, with films like **The Cove** (2009) and **Chasing Ice** (2012) employing sophisticated cinematography and narrative techniques to make complex issues accessible. **The Last Mountain** follows this tradition while adding crucial historical context about Appalachia's complex relationship with coal mining, dating back to the violent labor conflicts documented in John Sayles' dramatic film **Matewan** (1987). SUBHEAD: Corporate Power vs Community Activism

While **The Last Mountain** focuses on one valley's fight, it connects to broader documentaries exposing corporate environmental damage like **Company Town** (2016) and **Crude** (2009). The film's emphasis on grassroots activism mirrors other powerful documentaries like **When Two Worlds Collide** (2016) about indigenous resistance to Peruvian rainforest exploitation. Director Haney's approach of following both activists and affected community members creates an intimate portrait of environmental justice in action.
